fact.en: Trap 1: Evergreening of Patents: TRIPS mandates 20-year patents. Developing countries (e.g., India under Section 3(d) of Patents Act) block **evergreening** (securing minor variations of existing drugs to extend patents). Beware of assumptions that all countries permit patent extensions for minor chemical modifications.
fact.hi: Trap 1: Evergreening of Patents: TRIPS mandates 20-year patents. Developing countries (e.g., India under Section 3(d) of Patents Act) block **evergreening** (securing minor variations of existing drugs to extend patents). Beware of assumptions that all countries permit patent extensions for minor chemical modifications.

fact.en: Trap 2: Technology Leapfrogging: Leapfrogging doesn't mean skipping scientific research. It means bypassing physical developmental infrastructure (e.g., landline phone lines) to jump straight to advanced technologies (e.g., mobile networks, digital payment DPI).
fact.hi: Trap 2: Technology Leapfrogging: Leapfrogging doesn't mean skipping scientific research. It means bypassing physical developmental infrastructure (e.g., landline phone lines) to jump straight to advanced technologies (e.g., mobile networks, digital payment DPI).

fact.en: Trap 3: GERD/GDP Ratio: While India is a major space and software power, its Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) sits low at ~0.65% of GDP, compared to 2.5-4.8% in developed nations. Do not assume high absolute S&T output matches a high R&D-to-GDP investment ratio.
fact.hi: Trap 3: GERD/GDP Ratio: While India is a major space and software power, its Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) sits low at ~0.65% of GDP, compared to 2.5-4.8% in developed nations. Do not assume high absolute S&T output matches a high R&D-to-GDP investment ratio.

fact.en: Trap 4: Compulsory Licensing: Under TRIPS Doha Declaration, developing countries have the right to issue **Compulsory Licenses** to local generic firms during national health emergencies. This is a legal option, not an intellectual property violation.
